title: Firuz and His Wife (தமிழ்)

full_text:
Firuz was an honorable and trusted minister of state in ancient Persia, whose wife was celebrated across the capital for her peerless beauty, modest dignity, and intelligence.

One afternoon, the King, while riding through the city, stopped before Firuz’s mansion and asked for a cup of water. Firuz’s wife received her monarch with serene composure, served him cool water from behind the lattice, and spoke with such refined elegance that the King was tempted by selfish desire.

However, the noble lady smiled with dignified gravity and said: 'Sire, if an imperial lion enters a humble gazelle’s garden, will he trample the delicate lilies, or will his royal majesty protect the flowers from the wild beasts?'

The King was struck to his soul by the delicate reprimand. Filled with shame, he left his royal ring upon the divan as a token of reverence and departed with clean hands.

When Firuz returned, he found the King’s ring, and dark suspicions troubled his mind; he withdrew from his wife in silence.

The lady brought the matter before the King’s public tribunal in an allegorical petition: 'O King! I possessed a fertile garden which I tended with honor. A lion entered my garden and departed without breaking a single reed; yet my husband refuses to enter his orchard in fear of the lion’s paw!'

The King stood before the court and declared: 'The lion entered your garden, O lady, and found it guarded by angels of virtue; he departed with bowed head! Let your husband return with joyous pride.'

Firuz understood the truth, embraced his virtuous wife, and praised the wisdom that had preserved their domestic honor.
moral: Delicate allegories of honor and mutual respect preserve the sanctity of the home. [TA]
